The ADAPT Lab provides opportunities for current CCNY undergraduate and graduate students to become meaningfully involved in the research we do as a research assistant (RA).

We are a great fit for students interested in research in at least one of the following topic areas: stress, coping, trauma, couples, intimate partner violence, LGBTQ+ mental health, and psychotherapy research.

Students working in the lab can expect to receive training and direct experience in the following areas depending on current ongoing projects: theories and methods in stress and relationship science, study recruitment, project administration, data collection (including longitudinal and behavioral observation methods), data management, observational coding, statistical analysis, and for motivated students, manuscript writing and publication.

To apply to be an RA in the ADAPT Lab, please reach out directly to Dr. Sullivan (tsullivan1@ccny.cuny.edu) with a brief blurb about you, why you want to work in the lab, and what types of experience you'd hope to gain. Please include a current resume or CV and "ADAPT Lab: RA Position Inquiry" in the title. You should be willing to commit to at least two semesters in the lab. RAs can serve on a volunteer basis or receive course credit for their work in the lab.

Dr. Sullivan does not currently serve as a primary mentor for PhD students in the Clinical Psychology Program at CCNY or in the Health Psychology and Clinical Science Program at The Graduate Center at CUNY. He does not review applications for these programs, but he is open to serving on dissertation committees and to mentoring thesis projects for current CCNY master's students.
